summary: This Docker Compose configuration sets up a service called 'dood' that runs as an unprivileged user while still having access to Docker. It passes build arguments to customize the user and group IDs, then runs the container with those IDs and adds it to an extra Docker group so it can communicate with the Docker daemon on the host.

explanations.7: This uses parameter expansion syntax — if DOCKER_OS_GROUPID environment variable is set, use it; otherwise default to 1000. The same pattern repeats for the other build arguments.
explanations.10: The user field sets which user account runs the container, using the same default pattern. The format is userid:groupid.
explanations.13: group_add lets you add the container to additional groups beyond its primary group, which allows access to resources owned by those groups.
explanations.15: This adds the container to a Docker group (usually GID 1001 by default) so the unprivileged user inside can communicate with the Docker daemon socket mounted on line 17.
